# The Platform Experience Adoption Register

**Version:** 1.0.0 · **Updated:** 2026-07-19 · **Owner:** Colin Clapson

> **UIA § 17:** *"Every canonical building block carries a visible register: what it owns,
> which surfaces have adopted it, which are exempt and why. **Authored-but-unadopted must be
> impossible to hide.** The register lives beside the implementation (it is operational, not
> architectural); its existence is mandated here."*

This is that register. It is **operational, not architectural**: it creates no law, and every
rule it enforces belongs to a document listed below. It is **present tense** — it describes the
codebase as it is now, and it is *corrected*, never superseded. A stale row is a defect.

**It is not a document that can quietly go stale.** It *declares*; the code is *measured* against
it, on every run, by `scripts/ci/adoption-register-gate.ts` — which fails CI when a canonical owner
loses its last consumer, when a rival count rises above a ceiling below, when a retired predecessor
returns, or when a new module appears with no importers. Run `npm run adoption:check` to see where
the codebase actually stands. This file is generated from `adoption-register.json`, its single
source of truth; the gate fails if the two ever disagree, so the prose can never drift from the data.

**Governed by:** [THA_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md §17](../../architecture/THA_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md) (the mandate) · [THA_EXPERIENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md](../../architecture/THA_EXPERIENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md) (EXP1/EXP2) · [ENGINEERING_WORKFLOW.md](../../architecture/ENGINEERING_WORKFLOW.md) (Adoption Register Compliance) · [PX1](./PX1_PLATFORM_EXPERIENCE_DISCOVERY_AND_ARCHITECTURE.md) §6 (the specification)

---

## 1. Canonical owners

**Enforcement** says whether the row is machine-checked or human-reviewed. It is stated per row
rather than implied, so the gap between what is *declared* and what is *enforced* is visible on
the day the register is created, rather than discovered months after it started costing something
(PKCA Rule KC8).

**There are no adoption counts in this document, deliberately.** A count in prose is a count that
rots: it is correct on the day it is typed and wrong by the next commit, and a register that
carries stale numbers teaches its readers not to trust it. The live counts are measured from the
code on every run — `npm run adoption:check` prints them, and fails the build when one of them
breaks a rule below. **The document declares; the gate measures.**

**NORTH3 (2026-07-17) — `.text-signature` moved from `@layer utilities` to `@layer components`, and that CHANGED ITS CONTRACT.** The role was declared inside `@layer utilities` at index.css:593 — *after* `@tailwind utilities` at line 10. A role and a Tailwind utility are both single-class selectors, so specificity ties and **source order decided**: the role won every contest, always, and any utility aimed at it was dead on arrival. It was not a starting point; it was a cage, and it was silent about it. **Home's own signature carried `leading-[1.02]` and measured 1.15** — this role's own line-height, to the decimal. The same defect had already killed NORTH2's `title-page font-normal` on the salutation beside it (see `type-roles` below). The role now sits in `components`, which is the relationship Tailwind's layer order (base → components → utilities) exists to express: **components name a thing, utilities adjust it.** This admits no new pattern under UIA § 17 — it applies the pattern the layer system already had to the one block that had opted out of it. `.text-signature` remains the ONE entry point to the third voice and its permitted-surface rule is **byte-unchanged**: moving a role's layer changes what a permitted surface may ADJUST, never who may USE it. | ✅ governed | review |

Rank is carried at night by tint and border: the same hierarchy, a different instrument. Study A had independently reached that answer. This closes Blueprint § 18 open item 4 for this vocabulary. **The ambient light pool declares a ceiling, not a pairing** (`--light-ambient-ceiling`), per the § 15 rule ODL2 added: a graded surface carrying no text has no colour pairing to measure, so it names the strength it may never exceed instead — which is what EXP4 asked for when it flagged its own radial pool as needing *"a named token with a stated ceiling"*.

**ADOPTED BY HOME'S E3 (NORTH1, 2026-07-17), and the reference is deleted.** This row's open migration is DISCHARGED, by the trigger it named rather than by anyone deciding it had waited long enough. `client/src/pages/home-experience-page.tsx` now stands on the ground plane, the warm shadows, the rim of light and the radius ladder, and it is a surface a household lands on. `pages/dev/material-a-warm-layers.tsx` and `scripts/capture-exp4-materiality-depth.ts` were deleted in that same change, which completes the disposition EXP4 § 6 set for all three studies: B and C lost the selection and died at ODL2, A won, graduated into UIA § 4, served as the vocabulary's reference implementation for exactly as long as it had no rival, and died the day a real room adopted it. No study outlived its own decision.

**NORTH2 (2026-07-17) — the values were RE-VALUED, and the law was not touched.** Every surface this row owns was `hsl(0 0% 100%)` — pure white, zero hue, zero saturation — in a room whose only light is a warm morning (`--light-rim: 48 60% 98%`). That is not a material; it is the absence of a decision, and it was the single strongest reason Home read as a beautiful web application rather than a room. No natural material is pure white: plaster, linen, oak and stone all carry hue and saturation, and a surface standing in warm light takes the colour of the light that falls on it. So: `--surface-primary` and `--card` → plaster `42 46% 98%`; `--surface-support` → linen over the counter, and MORE translucent (0.65 → 0.34) so the counter shows THROUGH the doors; `--ground-plane` → warmer stone at 0.82; `--surface-primary-border` → a joint rather than a drawn ring (7 lightness points off its fill → under 4). **The value RANGE narrowed deliberately** (canvas 95→94, card 100→98, saturation 27→46 RISING toward the light): planes are now read from the shadow beneath them and the rim of light along their top edge — which is how a real counter is read against a real wall — and never from a jump to a foreign colour. **`--shadow-support` INVERTED**: support was a drop-shadowed card floating ON the counter; it is now ETCHED INTO it (inset warm shadow at the top lip only — never four-sided, which is the disabled-input tell — plus a light rim on the lower lip, which is the one edge of a groove that faces the sun and the one line a disabled control never has). Hover lifts it out of the groove to meet the hand; press seats it back. **No law changed.** UIA §7 fixes the semantic STRUCTURE (one definition source, no raw colour in a surface, one meaning per colour) and every clause still holds — same named roles, same one place, and not one surface gained a colour of its own. §7 never fixed the VALUES, and the values were what was wrong. Authorised platform-wide by Colin Clapson (2026-07-17); scoping it to Home would have forked the one visual language UIA §17 forbids forking. **Verified beyond Home**: Planner, Cookbook, Pantry, Shopping and Dashboard captured at 1440×900 and inspected — no contrast or legibility regression (`docs/ui-audit/north2-home/rooms/`). Dark mode is a separate value set (§7) and is byte-untouched: it derives `--surface-primary` from its own `--card`, and its shadows were already `none`. | ✅ governed | machine |

It owns the CLOCK, not the VOICE — the three strings are grandfathered debt owned by INT21 and scheduled as CP3 (THA_BEHAVIOUR_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md §9). | ✅ governed | machine |

Reads GET /api/planner/current-week, which is server/lib/household-planner-week.ts over resolvePlannerWeek (shared/time/household-time.ts). Derives nothing: the client renders household time, never derives it (HT12). | ✅ governed | machine |
| 45 | **Type roles (the named voices of the type scale)** | `index.css (.title-page, .title-section, .title-card, .text-table, .text-numeric)` | The named type roles of **UIA § 8**'s scale — the classes a surface uses instead of picking a size and a weight. `.title-page` (32/38, 600) · `.title-section` (22/28, 600) · `.title-card` (16/22, 500) · `.text-table` (13/18) · `.text-numeric` (18/24, 600). A surface names the ROLE; the role names the numbers, once. This is UIA § 16's *"surfaces speak semantic only"* applied to type, and it is why a raw `text-[22px] font-semibold` in a surface is a defect.

**This row was created by NORTH3 (2026-07-17) and the owner it describes is not new — it is years old and had simply never been registered.** UIA § 17 requires every canonical building block to carry a visible register row, and five of THA's type roles did not have one; the sibling `.text-signature` (the third voice) has had a row since UXHOME1, so the scale was half-registered and nobody could see the gap. Creating this row **admits no new pattern and adds no law** — it records an owner that every surface in the product has been consuming all along. It is `review`, not `machine`: NORTH3 has not authored a machine check for it, and asserting one it had not validated would be worse than the silence it replaces.

**NORTH3 MOVED THESE ROLES FROM `@layer utilities` TO `@layer components`, AND THAT IS A CONTRACT CHANGE.** They were declared inside `@layer utilities` at index.css:593 — *after* `@tailwind utilities` at line 10. A role and a Tailwind utility are both single-class selectors (0,1,0), so specificity ties and **source order decided every contest: the role always won.** Any utility aimed at a role was dead on arrival, silently, with no error, no warning, and no way to see it except by measuring the rendered page.

**Two of Home's shipped, deliberate, carefully-argued intentions had already been killed by it, and both were discovered by measuring rather than by reading:**

1. **NORTH2's salutation.** It re-voiced "Welcome home," to `title-page font-normal` and wrote a paragraph explaining why the household's NAME must be the loudest thing in the room, quoting UIA § 8's own rule that *"shouting in bold is spending the emphasis budget on the shout"*. `.title-page`'s `font-weight: 600` beat `font-normal`. **The salutation shipped semibold — the exact thing the change was written to stop — and the comment describing the fix outlived the fix.**
2. **Home's signature.** It carries `leading-[1.02]` to pull the hand tight to the name. It measured **1.15** — `.text-signature`'s own line-height, to the decimal.

Both are now live and both were verified in the **compiled production CSS**, not merely in source: `.font-normal` at byte 70923 and `.leading-\[1\.02\]` at 71400 both fall after `.title-page` (18212) and `.text-signature` (18604). Measured in the browser: the salutation went 600 → **400**, and the signature's box went 101px → **90px** (88 × 1.02).

**The blast radius was measured before the move, and it is one surface.** A grep of every `title-page|title-section|title-card` in `client/src` for an adjacent font-weight or font-size utility returns exactly ONE hit — home-experience-page.tsx:576, NORTH2's `font-normal`. Nothing else in the codebase attempts to override a role, so nothing else can change when overriding starts working. Verified by looking as well: the five other rooms (planner · cookbook · pantry · shopping · dashboard) were captured before and after and are **byte-identical**, except the dashboard, which was proven by isolation to have drifted from the concurrent CONV1 P9 session's Stories-engine edits and **not** from this change — with the CSS reverted the dashboard still differed from its baseline, and with the CSS applied versus reverted it was byte-identical.

**What did NOT move:** `.scrollbar-hide`, `.text-premium` and `.calm-table` stayed in `@layer utilities`, because they are genuine utilities and component styles respectively. Only the six roles moved (the five here plus `.text-signature`, which keeps its own row), because only they are roles.

**The rule this row exists to carry:** *a role is a starting point, not a cage.* A surface that names a role and then adjusts one property of it is using the scale correctly, and it must be able to. If a role ever needs to be un-overridable, that is a decision to state out loud in this register — never a side-effect of which `@layer` block someone happened to paste it into. | ✅ governed | review |

Owns the room-scoping (`domains`), the cap, the eyebrow and the honest-absence rule: nothing learned yet renders nothing, never an empty-state placeholder implying something is missing. HOUSE_ACT2 Door 1 moved it from one household-wide mount on Profile to five — Profile keeps the unfiltered view; Planner, Pantry, Shopping and Cookbook each show only the Patterns learned from behaviour in that room. Filtering is client-side over the ONE shared query, mirroring AmbientIntelligence: a per-room server query would fragment a cache the hook already holds in full. | ✅ governed | machine |

It also owns the placeholder notice, which is what stops THA publishing an invented company number without saying so. ## 2. Rivals — the ratchet

Each count is a **ceiling measured from the code**. The gate fails if a count rises: a competing
implementation cannot enter THA without someone raising the ceiling here, by hand, with a reason.
That is the whole mechanism by which *"future work cannot introduce competing implementations
without explicit ownership"* is true rather than hoped for.

| Concern | Rival | Ceiling | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dialog | `<DrawerContent>` — a second overlay container chosen per-file | 11 | Capped. New overlays use `Overlay`, which decides sheet-vs-dialog by viewport. |
| Dialog | `<SheetContent>` — a third | 3 | Capped. `Sheet` is retired as a *choice*; it survives only as Overlay's mobile implementation. |
| Loading state | Hand-rolled `animate-pulse` loading surfaces | 9 | The owner carries the class internally; these are the copies outside it. PX1-W4.8 retired the 12 verbatim Skeleton clones. |
| Loading state | `<Loader2>` usages | 175 | Capped, not banned: 140 are the exempt inline pending mark above. The population may fall, never rise. BUS1 raised 179 → 181: two `<Loader2>` marks on Privacy Settings, both INSIDE a control (the data-download button and the account-deletion confirm button) while an indeterminate request is in flight. That is the usage this concern's own rule assigns to Loader2 rather than to Skeleton — 'Skeleton owns content arriving; Loader2 owns indeterminate work inside a control' — so the ceiling is raised rather than the marks replaced. Content-arriving states on that page use Skeleton, as the rule requires. |
| Mutation feedback | Raw `useMutation` — feedback owned by the call site | 132 | Not all are defects: a mutation with no household-visible outcome owes no toast. Capped so the population cannot grow. |
| Button / primary action | Raw `<button>` elements outside the design system | 454 | Each reinvents press feedback and misses the touch floor. Capped: the population may fall, never rise. |
| Time-of-day greeting | An ambient hour read reaching a greeting word — the shape all four retired copies shared | 0 | Zero, and it stays zero. THA_HOUSEHOLD_TIME_ARCHITECTURE.md §16 names this gate by name: 'the gate that matters is the one that fails when someone writes a sixth getGreeting()'. Also ratcheted in the publication register (household-time / ht-no-rival-greeting), mutation-tested. |

## 3. Exemptions — explicit, with a reason

*"Any surface exempt from a canonical owner is exempt in the register, with a reason — never
silently."* (UIA § 17)

| Concern | Exempt surface | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation | All pages except `/home` | No page imports the nav directly — `WorkspaceHeader` mounts it. Home is the one page that imports this module, and it imports the LIST rather than the nav: it renders four rooms as doors on its counter and reads their hrefs, labels and glyphs from here. Three importers is the correct number, not a high one — the alternative was a fourth copy of the house's room list. |
| Form field | ~20 hand-rolled `useState` forms | They now carry real labels and accessible names (PX1-W4.1), so the household-visible defect is closed. `ui/form.tsx`'s RHF context is not worth forcing onto a two-field dialog; what mattered was the accessible name, and `warnIfUnlabelled` now enforces that at the primitive — see `accessible-name`. |
| Accessible name enforcement | `ui/input.tsx`, `ui/textarea.tsx` only | Two importers is the whole design: the warning belongs at the two primitives every field passes through, not at 300 call sites. |
| Loading state | `Loader2` as an **inline pending mark** — the spinner inside a control that is working (140 of its 180 usages), and the route-transition fallback in `App.tsx` | A skeleton answers *"what is about to appear here"*. A button that is saving has nothing to shape a skeleton around, and a route fallback must not paint a skeleton of a page it cannot yet know. For *work inside a control*, Loader2 is the right mark and Skeleton would be the wrong one. |
| Error boundary | Mounted once, in `App.tsx` | One importer is the correct number: a boundary is mounted at the shell, not per page. |
| Unsaved-work guard | Profile only | Profile is the only dirty→Save surface in THA; everywhere else commits on interaction. One consumer is the correct number, not a low one. |
| Meal presentation (the core noun) | `PlannerMealCard.tsx` | It owns the thumbnail-*less* planner-cell face, which is a different object with a different job. It was `MealCard`'s seed, not its rival. |
| Back | Pantry, Diary, Nutrition | They are bottom-nav destinations, not subpages. A back affordance on a root destination is a lie about the hierarchy. |
| "The meal library changed" | Per-meal keys — `['/api/meals', mealId, 'nutrition']` and similar | These address one meal, not the library. They are correct, and the pattern above deliberately does not match them: it anchors on the closing bracket, so only the *bare library keys* are forbidden. PX1-W3's own grep looked for the double-quoted form only, which is how four single-quoted `['/api/meals']` invalidations survived a workstream that reported zero. |
| Bottom-nav clearance | Shop mode's two fullscreen scrollers | `fixed inset-0` genuinely *escapes* `<main>`, so the owner is applied at the point of escape. This is the one legitimate re-application; the six decorative duplicates were removed in PX1-W4b.5. |
| Signature typography (the third voice) | Every household-facing surface EXCEPT `/home` | Not an exemption from the owner — an exemption from USING it, and it is now the rule rather than the gap. **The ADOPT ruling (Colin Clapson, 2026-07-17, recorded by ODL2) was EXECUTED by NORTH1 on the same day**: `/home` is the one permitted surface, and the one thing on it in the signature voice is the household's own name in the greeting — Home's single ornament (Blueprint § 12.1), and data-borne. Caveat is loaded from the `@import` in `client/src/index.css`, which is the first time a household downloads it. The rarity is the whole point: the voice is never a button, a label, a status, or a value a household reads in order to act. A second permitted surface is a governed decision, named here one at a time, and there is no second one. |
| Legal document presentation | client/src/pages/legal-page.tsx sub-processor table | The sub-processor list is not a clause of the document — it is generated from shared/legal/subprocessors.ts, which is read out of the code, and it renders as cards rather than as prose blocks. Putting it through the block renderer would have required a fifth block kind that exactly one document uses. |

## 6. Authored-but-unadopted — the orphan ratchet

A module under these roots with **zero importers** is authored-but-unadopted — the failure state UIA §17 exists to end, and the mechanism behind PX1's `PageHeader.tsx` (a full unadopted successor to `WorkspaceHeader`, sitting live-looking in the tree for a future workstream to adopt *instead of* the real owner). PX1-W4.7 deleted 26 such files. These are what the gate found **after** that sweep — none of them known to any PX1 workstream, all of them found by the register on the day it was built. They are recorded as **defects, not exemptions**: an exemption says "this is fine", and these are not fine. They are simply no longer hidden. The gate fails on a *new* one. This is the same shape as `typecheck:ci`'s recorded baseline of 168 known errors: a number that may fall and may never rise.

The gate fails on a **new** orphan. These are the known ones, each named and owned. They are

## 7. How to change this register

1. **Adopting an owner** — migrate the consumer, then `npm run adoption:record` to tighten the ceiling.
2. **Introducing a new owner** — add a concern row naming what it owns, its predecessor, and its
   first consumers. An owner with no consumers fails the gate, by design: it is not permitted to
   author a foundation and adopt it later.
3. **Retiring a predecessor** — migrate every consumer, delete it, and add it to § 4 in the same
   change. The gate then keeps it dead.
4. **Needing an exception** — raise the ceiling in § 2 or add an exemption in § 3, *with a reason*.
   This is deliberately a visible, reviewable edit rather than a silent one.
